title: Rights & responsibilities of citizens
examples: What is the difference between a right and a responsibility?
Can I make a difference in my local community?
Are there ways I can participate even if I am young?

explain.say: Today we learn about being a good citizen. A citizen has rights and also has responsibilities.
Participation means taking part in community life. You can participate by voting when you are old enough.
Volunteering means giving your time freely to help others. You might help clean up a local park for free.
A concrete example of participation is joining a school council. You can help decide on new school rules.

items: Student Council Member | Suggesting a new lunch option

explain.say: Another example is volunteering at a local animal shelter. You can spend time walking the dogs there.
In real life, if your street needs more recycling bins, you can organize a local clean-up day. This shows both action and care.

faq.q: What is the difference between a right and a responsibility?
faq.a: A right is something you are allowed to have or do. A responsibility is something you should do for others or your community.
asks: Do I have to have rights?
What are my duties as a citizen?

faq.q: Can I make a difference if I am still in primary school?
faq.a: Yes, you can make a difference through actions like recycling or helping a neighbour. Small actions build big change over time.
asks: How can kids help their community?
Do I need to be old to help?

faq.a: No, participation can mean speaking up in class or joining a local group. It means getting involved in decisions.
asks: Is voting the only way to participate?

faq.q: What are some good places to volunteer?
faq.a: You can volunteer at libraries, animal shelters, or community gardens. These places always need helping hands.
asks: Are all places good for volunteering?

faq.q: If I speak up about a problem, will anyone listen?
faq.a: If you speak clearly and with good ideas, people are more likely to listen. Good ideas need good presentation.
asks: How do I get people to listen?

facts: Citizens have rights that protect them from unfair treatment.
Responsibilities include obeying laws and caring for the environment.
Participation means taking part in the life of your community.
Volunteering gives your time to help others without payment.

quiz.show: Picking up litter in a park.

options.show: Telling a friend to pick it up.
options.say: Telling a friend to pick it up.

options.show: Picking up litter in a park.
options.say: Picking up litter in a park.

options.show: Waiting for a park worker to clean it.
options.say: Waiting for a park worker to clean it.

options.show: Taking a photo and posting it online.
options.say: Taking a photo and posting it online.

quiz.why: This is a direct action that shows care for the shared environment.

wrong.0: This passes the responsibility to someone else.
wrong.2: This is passive and does not show personal responsibility.

quiz.say: Joining a school committee to suggest a new rule is an example of:
quiz.why: It shows you are actively taking part in making decisions.

wrong.0: It is an action you take, not something you are automatically given.
wrong.1: A law is mandatory; this is voluntary involvement.
wrong.3: Volunteering is giving time, not necessarily influencing rules.

quiz.say: Which of these activities is purely volunteering?
quiz.show: Reading to children at the library.

options.show: Following the rules of the playground.
options.say: Following the rules of the playground.

options.show: Reading to children at the library.
options.say: Reading to children at the library.

quiz.why: You are giving your time freely to help the community.

wrong.0: While civic, voting is a specific right, not just general time-giving.
wrong.1: This is following a rule, which is a responsibility, not giving time.
wrong.3: This is usually required by the school, not freely given.
